'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Iraqi conflict]]
**[[Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq (2025–2026)|Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq]]
***[[United States Armed Forces|American troops]] complete their withdrawal from [[Iraq]], ending their 23-year presence in the country that started with the [[2003 invasion of Iraq|2003 U.S. invasion]], and also the 12-year [[Operation Inherent Resolve|U.S. intervention]] against the [[Islamic State]] in Iraq and [[Syria]]. [https://apnews.com/article/iraq-us-withdrawal-militias-disarmament-kurds-a097a39f3d1a3515adc2ba3298a6816f (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-forces-exit-iraq-emboldening-irans-proxies-islamic-state-2026-09-30/ (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir]]
**Hashim Moosa, a top [[Lashkar-e-Taiba]] commander and the mastermind of the [[2025 Pahalgam attack]] is killed in an encounter with security forces in [[Budgam]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)| Jammu and Kashmir]].[https://www.newindianexpress.com/amp/story/india/2026/Sep/29/let-terrorist-hashim-moosa-wanted-in-pahalgam-attack-killed-in-jks-budgam-2026-09-30/ (The New Indian Express)]
*[[Aftermath of the Syrian civil war]]
**Unknown gunmen [[Mass shooting|open fire]] against a bus carrying employees returning home from work in [[Homs]], [[Syria]], killing seven people and wounding four more. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/syria-hit-gas-explosion-deadly-bus-attack-and-israeli-shelling (Middle East Eye)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance]]
**A [[United States federal judge]] approves [[Mass media in the United States|media]] conglomerate [[Paramount Skydance]]'s [[Settlement (litigation)|settlement]] with 12 [[U.S. state|state]]s that challenged its [[Mergers and acquisitions|acquisition]] of [[Warner Bros. Discovery]] on [[United States antitrust law|antitrust grounds]], allowing the [[United States dollar|$]]81 billion merger to proceed toward completion. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/entertainment/showbiz/movies-series/2026/10/1/us-judge-accepts-paramount-s-warner-bros-buyout-settlement-1006 (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A helicopter crashes in [[Marondera]], [[Zimbabwe]], killing all six people on board, including businessman [[Wicknell Chivayo]] and his wife. '''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in the United States]]
**[[Capital punishment in Tennessee]]
***The [[U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit]] halts [[Christa Pike]]'s [[execution]] in [[Tennessee]] shortly before it was scheduled, to allow for further review of whether evidence of [[Child sexual abuse laws in the United States|childhood sexual abuse]] was adequately considered at sentencing; the [[United States Supreme Court|U.S. Supreme Court]] shortly after lifts the Sixth Circuit's [[Stay of execution|stay order]], allowing the execution to proceed. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260930-court-halts-tennessee-s-first-execution-of-woman-in-200-years (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/tennessee-due-execute-woman-first-time-two-centuries-2026-09-30/ (Reuters)]
***Pike is sent to a hospital following the failed administration of two rounds of the drugs used to perform the [[lethal injection]]. [https://www.axios.com/local/nashville/2026/10/01/chaos-questions-christa-pike-execution-attempt (''Axios'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cq8r6rjdvlx6o (BBC News)]
*[[2026 Turkish LGBTQ raids]], [[Censorship in Turkey]], [[Censorship of LGBTQ issues]]
**A [[Judicial system of Turkey|Turkish court]] orders the closure of independent [[Mass media in Turkey|news website]] ''[[T24 (newspaper)|T24]]'' and its social media accounts after the [[Ministry of Justice (Turkey)|justice ministry]] reported that ''T24'' had published 118 items during the previous year which the court classified as "[[LGBTQ propaganda]]". [https://today.rtl.lu/news/world/turkey-says-news-site-closed-for-lgbtq-propaganda-137222786 (AFP via RTL Today)]
*[[Flydubai Flight 1073]]
**A [[Flydubai]] flight from [[Dubai]], [[United Arab Emirates]], to [[Tel Aviv]], [[Israel]], is landed safely in [[Tabuk, Saudi Arabia|Tabuk]], [[Saudi Arabia]], by a [[In-flight crew relief|relief crew]] after the copilot violently attacked the captain in an attempted [[aircraft hijacking]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/cw980g1lem5pt (BBC News)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/09/30/world/live-news/dubai-israel-plane-flydubai-intl (CNN)]
*[[Arrest of Roger Mariaca]]
**[[Bolivian National Police|Bolivian police]] arrest [[attorney general]] Roger Mariaca and [[Santa Cruz de la Sierra]] prosecutor Alberto Zeballos after the [[U.S. State Department]] accused them of [[Corruption in Bolivia|corruption]] and links to [[Narcotics in Bolivia|drug trafficking]]. Police also raid prosecutors' offices in several cities. [https://www.afp.com/en/bolivia-arrests-attorney-general-roger-mariaca-government-source (AFP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Romanian political crisis]]
**[[Romania]]'s [[Parliament of Romania|parliament]] rejects [[Prime Minister of Romania|prime minister]]-designate [[Siegfried Mureșan]]'s proposed [[Government of Romania|government]], receiving 182 of the 233 votes required for approval, prolonging the [[political crisis]] that began after [[Ilie Bolojan]]'s [[Bolojan cabinet|government]] fell in May. [https://www.afp.com/en/romanian-parliament-rejects-pro-eu-pm-candidate-amid-political-deadlock (AFP)] [https://apnews.com/article/romania-europe-politics-eu-government-muresan-c3b4ce6345cc08904ffaa63aadc88ca7 (AP)]
*[[2026 French student protests|2026 French lycée protests]]
**At least 450 people are arrested and 76 people are injured after [[Education in France|students]] in [[France]] protest over class overcrowding and teacher shortages. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c862epne7glyo (BBC News)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/30/world/europe/france-student-protest-arrests.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[AI boom]]
**The [[Tokyo District Court]] rules that a person's voice can receive [[Copyright law of Japan|protection]] under [[publicity rights]], in [[Japan]]'s first case involving alleged [[audio deepfake]], while dismissing actor [[Kenjiro Tsuda]]'s request to remove already-deleted [[TikTok]] videos. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260930-japan-court-rules-human-voice-is-protected-in-tiktok-ai-case (AFP via France 24)]
